blockers.quote: Your oldest friend is beside you for the window-seat gag, so he is in the story early.
blockers.why: Check #9 Earned stakes fails. Mere presence and one gag do not earn the friend as the person you may lose at the choice.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Your oldest friend saves your window seat, splits the last chai with you, and notices the boss message you keep deleting. You ask nothing; he helps anyway."

blockers.quote: Then every question becomes a command: "can you pass the salt", "will you stay a bit", "do you agree"; the tags flip faster
blockers.why: Check #6 Every use has a gap fails. These requests produce exactly the compliance you now expect.
blockers.fix: Replace with: "Every question overshoots: ‘can you pass the salt?’ and every hand reaches; ‘will you stay a bit?’ and your friend sits while watching the door; ‘do you agree?’ and the meeting becomes unanimously useless."

blockers.quote: Foot-in-the-door (Freedman and Fraser, 1966): a small yes makes a larger one more likely
blockers.why: Check #13 Every fact moves the story fails. The power already guarantees both requests, so this fact neither causes nor changes the boss beat.
blockers.fix: Cut this fact and let the boss sequence turn on the emotional gap: you receive the project you wanted but cannot know whether you earned it.

suggestions.quote: a meeting where your idea goes through without a single hand up; a stage; a crowd.
suggestions.fix: Make this one causal sequence: the meeting approves your idea, therefore it reaches the stage, but the crowd's automatic agreement lets your worst version proceed and drives your friend to leave.

suggestions.quote: one sentence, "stay?", would keep him in the room. The power, or the person.
suggestions.fix: Give using the power a defensible benefit: make the friend the only person who can stop the harmful approved project, so letting him leave respects him while asking him to stay protects the team.

suggestions.quote: the power barely changed anyone; they were always far more willing to say yes than you believed
suggestions.fix: Reserve this broader discovery for the late turn. At minute three establish only that strangers were kinder than expected; here reveal through the friend and mother that the people closest to you had also been choosing yes freely.

keep.quote: The viewer is not waiting for a bigger power; they are waiting for a smaller room.
you have not won a single argument this week, you have ended them.
Three dots. For once, you don't know what's coming.
